js.lean: No strong side: the ratings like Minnesota more than the line does, but Edwards is questionable and MIN is on a back-to-back, so the +4.5 is a small lean at most and a pass until Edwards' status is known.
why: Opponent-adjusted net rating is MIN +5.9 against CLE +0.5 (3 and 2 games). The ratings-only margin has MIN ahead by about 2 even after home court, while DraftKings has CLE -4.5. MIN's raw numbers are strong: 121.0 scored and 97.7 allowed per game, with ORB% 0.361 against CLE's defensive rebounding of 0.226 allowed-side ORB%. CLE turns it over often (TOV% 0.199), but it gets to the line (FT rate 0.398).

Samples are tiny, 3 games for MIN and 2 for CLE, and the ratings are shrunk toward average. MIN's three wins came against TOR, ORL and MIA, so the 5.9 net could be overstated. The market line carries most of the weight, so I keep both adjustments at 0.
risks: Edwards (knee) is questionable. He averages 28.7 points on 31.3 minutes, and the line may already price in his absence. If he sits, MIN's margin and total probably drop.
MIN is on the second night of a back-to-back, while CLE has 1 day of rest. The data gives no measured fatigue effect, so I did not adjust for it, but it is a real risk to minutes and efficiency.
Very small samples for both teams, with several new rosters (Kuminga, Ball, Dosunmu, Harden), so early ratings are unstable.
matchups: CLE defense allows forwards +10% threes per minute, which helps Kuminga and McDaniels three-point volume (small sample).
MIN defense allows centers +7% threes and +9% assists, which is a mild plus for Allen and Mobley passing and shooting touches.
MIN defense is tougher on guards (-11% threes allowed) and forwards (-12% threes allowed), a slight negative for Mitchell and Harden from deep.
